# Executable standards coverage

<!-- Generated by npm run conformance:docs. Edit tests/conformance/matrix.json. -->

These are bounded acceptance claims, not a percentage of SysML conformance.
“Covered” means the listed assertions pass. A known gap must still fail its
named assertion; new failures or unexpected passes fail the run. Planned cases
are not executed and never counted as passing. Each area lists remaining scope.

Run `npm run conformance`. Results, engine/library pins, fixture hashes and
elapsed process times are written to `target/conformance/report.json`.
Each executable case gets a fresh native process and a 30-second deadline.
Clause references identify the source of a test, not complete coverage of that clause.

- [SysML 2.0 formal/2026-03-02](https://www.omg.org/spec/SysML/2.0/Language/PDF)
- [KerML 1.0 formal/2026-03-01](https://www.omg.org/spec/KerML/1.0/PDF)

## Coverage limits

- **Imports and visibility:** General metadata predicates and filtered imports, all contextual resolution rules, and complete implicit membership construction remain unqualified. Checked enumeration covers the bounded cases below; unknown results are not complete language conformance.
- **Typing:** Multiple and implicit typing, chained types and all type-kind constraints need further cases.
- **Specialization and inheritance:** Diamond coverage is limited to a common ancestor; conflicts, cycles and all inherited memberships require broader qualification.
- **Subsetting:** These cases check target identity, not instance-value containment or every conformance constraint.
- **Redefinition:** Direction, multiplicity, featuring-type conformance and nested redefinitions need additional cases.
- **Multiplicity:** Only literal declared bounds are asserted; expression bounds, effective defaults and containment are unqualified.
- **Conjugated port typing:** These assertions cover written references, not conjugated direction/flow semantics.
- **Connections and chains:** Endpoint identity and arity are covered; direction, flow compatibility and connection end conformance need further cases.
- **Names and source fidelity:** Byte/UTF-16 mapping and recovery are project API guarantees; lexical names are the standards link. No editable CST contract is claimed.
- **Cyclic input handling:** Termination is an operational guarantee, not a semantic verdict about every cycle. Continuous fuzzing remains separate work.
- **Lexical names and dialect boundaries:** These cases exercise reserved, quoted and escaped names; all terminals, escape forms and grammar alternatives remain unqualified.

## Known failures and planned work


The authored fixtures are in `tests/conformance/fixtures`. Official examples are
copied unchanged from the pinned release; see `tests/conformance/upstream/provenance.json`
and its README. The corpus probe does not execute the Java pilot implementation.
